'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[William Cohen]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Susan Collins]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsME}} The '''1996 United States Senate election in Maine''' was held November 5, 1996. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[William Cohen]] was tapped by the Clinton administration to serve as Secretary of Defense. To replace him, [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Joseph E. Brennan]] won the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary while political consultant [[Susan Collins]] won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary. A competitive general election ensued, but Collins ultimately won out over Brennan, keeping the seat in the Republican column. With Collins' election to the Senate in 1996, Maine became the third state after California and Kansas to have two sitting female senators, and the first to have two elected female Republican senators. Brennan and Collins both ran in the [[1994 Maine gubernatorial election|1994 gubernatorial election]], and each won their respective party's nomination, but lost the general election to independent [[Angus King]], who would be elected in Maine's other Senate seat in [[2012 United States Senate election in Maine|2012]] and become a Senator in 2013, serving alongside Collins. Following his departure from the Senate, Cohen was appointed [[United States Secretary of Defense]] by President [[Bill Clinton]] from 1997 to 2001. This was the last U.S. Senate election in Maine to see a Democrat carry any Maine county until [[2020 United States Senate election in Maine|2020]], when Collins lost [[Cumberland County, Maine|Cumberland]] and [[Knox County, Maine|Knox]] counties to [[Sara Gideon]]; Collins was re-elected in 16-county landslides in [[2002 United States Senate election in Maine|2002]], [[2008 United States Senate election in Maine|2008]], and [[2014 United States Senate election in Maine|2014]], while Maine's other seat saw similar 16-county landslides for Republican [[Olympia Snowe]] in [[2000 United States Senate election in Maine|2000]] and [[2006 United States Senate election in Maine|2006]] and for Independent Angus King in [[2012 United States Senate election in Maine|2012]]. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== * [[Joseph E. John Hathaway had sex with his twelve-year-old babysitter on multiple occasions in 1990.{{Cite web |title=Maine Senate candidate fights sex charge - UPI Archives |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1996/06/06/Maine-Senate-candidate-fights-sex-charge/5437834033600/ |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=UPI |language=en}} Hathaway vehemently denied the allegations, and blamed opponent Robert A.G. Monks for planting the story,{{Cite news |last=Rimer |first=Sara |date=1996-06-06 |title=POLITICS: THE SENATE;Maine Candidate Again Faces 1990 Child-Sex Accusation |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/06/06/us/politics-the-senate-maine-candidate-again-faces-1990-child-sex-accusation.html |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} though the mother of the girl corroborated it. Monks admitted to sending a private investigator to Hathaway's former residence of [[Huntsville, Alabama]] to look into the story. Ultimately, both stories proved to benefit Susan Collins, who won over 55% of the primary vote.{{Cite news |last=Weinsten |first=Joshua L. |title=Monks' cultivated reputation is gone with the election |work=The Portland Press Herald |quote=Allegations that W. John Hathaway sexually abused an adolescent girl harmed one of his rivals for the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate more than they hurt Hathaway. After spending $1.8 million of his own money, Robert A.G. Monks placed third in a three-person race for the nomination Tuesday. Hathaway, a one-term state senator tainted by accusations that he had sex with his children's babysitter several years ago, fared better, fin ishing second behind the winner, Susan Collins. The final, desperate week of the campaign was so bleak for Monks that he conceded defeat at 8:40 p.m. only 40 minutes after voters left the polls. On Monday, the day he ran a full-page advertisement in the Portland Press Herald, his campaign manager acknowledged Monks would likely lose. Monks' carefully cultivated reputation as a patrician candidate cut from the same cloth as Margaret Chase Smith and Edmund Muskie both of whom he ran against in the 1970s is gone. Now he is seen as having participated in the dirtiest campaign in modern Maine history. "It's a campaign and week unlike anything I've ever seen in Maine," said Sandy Maisel, a professor of political science at Colby College. "It was the lowest level that Maine politics have sunk to." Christian Potholm, a political sci-ence professor at Bowdoin College, said Monks "just fell down like a stone." The allegations about Hathaway broke last Wednesday in newspaper stories in the Portland Press Herald and The Boston Globe. Hathaway immediately took the offensive, accusing Monks of tipping the newspapers to the information that law enforcement officials in Alabama had investigated Hathaway for alleged sexual abuse of his chil dren's babysitter. Hathaway, who spent $600,000 of his own money on the campaign, effectively shifted the focus of the debate from his alleged sexual mis-conduct to what he described as Monks' role in making the allega tions public. During a press conference on Wednesday, an agitated, angry Monks railed about Hathaway's spin. But he acknowledged sending a pri-vate detective to Alabama, where the former state attorney general once investigated Hathaway's relationship with his children's babysitter. In his Tuesday night concession speech, Monks expressed wonder at the turn of events. Surrounded by the heaviest of Republican heavy hitters state Senate President Jeff Butland and House Republican Leader Walt Whitcomb, among others he said that "time and distance will offer me some vindication." He said that as recently as a week ago, he was in "a virtual dead heat" with Susan Collins, who won the nomination, slightly ahead. He fretted that Hathaway, who ran scathing television advertisements accusing Monks of "25 years of lies" was the real dirty trickster of the campaign. "People have lost trust in our polit- ical system today because they see their political leaders acting more and more like John Hathaway does," he said. But Monks himself had engaged in some negative campaigning. Among other things, he ran advertisements attacking Collins as a career bureaucrat. Many Mainers believed that by sending a private investigator to Alabama, Monks was playing dirty politics, Potholm said. "Whatever is true or not true about John Hathaway, people know that Bob Monks... hired a private investigator. It is the private investi-gator part that is souring Republican voters."}} ===Candidates=== * [[Susan Collins]], former Deputy Treasurer of Massachusetts and nominee for [[Governor of Maine|Governor]] in [[Maine gubernatorial election, 1994|1994]] * W.
